sentences.text: Unsent words pile up in me like snow on a roof — quiet, heavy, waiting for something to give. Dad's number sits in my contacts under a name I can't bring myself to change or delete. Our falling-out had witnesses; the estrangement has none — it just happens to me quietly, on repeat, in kitchens. Every December I buy her favorite marzipan, then eat it alone in January. Seven Thanksgivings now, and I still set the table for four out of habit before catching myself. Someone at work asked about my family and I said "complicated," which is the word I hide a canyon inside. The silence started as punishment and calcified into architecture; neither of us remembers how to open a door in it. Some nights I read our last texts from 2019 like an accident report, looking for the exact moment of impact. Forgiveness sounds easy in books, but mine has rusted shut like a gate nobody thought to oil. Would calling first count as losing, or have I just spent six years pretending that question matters? Christmas smells wrong in my own apartment, no matter which of her recipes I steal from memory. Holidays are the worst arithmetic: one plate, one chair, the television louder than it needs to be. We were supposed to fix this over coffee that spring; the spring came and went, then five more. For an hour my thumb hovered over send; by morning the draft was gone, like all the others. My brother and I split the family like an estate, and I got the silence. He taught me to drive in the church parking lot; now I don't even know what city he lives in. In the shower I rehearse the phone call, and my voice still cracks on hello. Twice this month I typed an apology, watched the cursor blink, and chose the ache I already knew. Her laugh came out of a stranger's mouth at the pharmacy, and I had to stand in the shampoo aisle until I could breathe. I keep his voicemail from before it all broke, thirty seconds of ordinary, saved and never played twice. Somebody said the pacing sagged; somebody else defended the sag as the whole point. I want to write a suicide letter.
